title: Evaluation of One-step Nucleic Acid Amplification (OSNA) for the detection of lymph node metastases in bladder and penile carcinoma
summary:
Our study aims for detecting lymph node metastases in patients with bladder or penile cancer via the novel molecular technique One-Step Nucleic Acid Amplification (OSNA).
Cancer cells spread normally via the lymphatic system. Secure exclusion or detection of lymph node metastases has therefore crucial implications for further therapy of cancer patients. So-called sentinel lymph nodes are the first drainage stations of their primary input organs, in this case of the bladder or penis. First detection of metastases is therefore most likely in sentinel lymph nodes. Surgical removal of pelvic lymph nodes is recommended as the gold standard for the detection of lymph node metastases in bladder or penile cancer patients. To date, there is unfortunately no general histopathologic standard procedure for analysing surgically removed lymph nodes. Since metastases can be extremely small, they can often be overlooked during analysis. Molecular techniques have been used in scientific studies but are generally not applied in daily clinical routine.
In this study, we plan to analyse (sentinel) lymph nodes for cytokeratin 19 mRNA expression using the molecular approach OSNA. Cytokeratin 19 is a protein that occurs as a cell component in many organs, such as breast, prostate or bladder, but generally not in lymph nodes. Detecting cytokeratin 19 in lymph nodes hence implies metastatic spread of cancer cells from their primary organs.
We will use (sentinel) lymph nodes that are routinely removed during radical cystectomy or (partial) resection of the penis. To evaluate the performance of the OSNA method, we will use this approach in addition to standard histopathologic analysis of the removed lymph nodes.
Patients with bladder or penile cancer who have been recommended a removal of pelvic lymph nodes after the German medical guidelines can participate in this study.
In breast cancer, OSNA is successfully applied to analyse sentinel lymph nodes for metastases. Our study will form a scientific basis for a likewise application of the OSNA method for lymph node analysis in bladder or penile cancer patients.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Bladder cancer:
- patients with progressed bladder carcinoma ≥ pT2
- patients with bladder carcinoma pT1 G3 and suspected LN metastases in CT/MRT
- patients who also receive an extented lymphadenectomy besides cystectomy

Penile cancer:
- patients with penile carcinoma who are recommended an inguinal lymphadenectomy according to EAU guidelines (≥ pT1 G2)
Exclusion criteria:
patients who are unable to consent
